items.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.summary: The paper proposes Ambient LLMs, a method that uses temperature matching to enable data‑efficient supervised fine‑tuning of large language models.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it reduces overfitting and data needs for fine‑tuning, improving model robustness.

items.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Spool introduces a low-latency streaming inference system for hybrid vision‑language models that efficiently handles sliding windows of recent video frames.
items.whyItMatters: It enables real‑time visual AI in accessibility and robotics, reducing latency and computational cost.

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.summary: StringQFT is an 18-volume, 3,795-page textbook series on string theory constructions of QFT, designed for AI-assisted research.
items.whyItMatters: Its comprehensive, AI-ready format could streamline advanced theoretical physics studies and accelerate discovery.

items.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method that ensures ε-surely feasible solutions for constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers faster, constraint‑respecting optimization for large-scale machine learning tasks.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.summary: The paper explores whether highly capable LLM agents can autonomously self‑improve without human‑defined improvement strategies.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding autonomous self‑optimization could reduce human oversight and accelerate AI development.

items.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
items.summary: The article critiques head-level bias attribution methods, showing they lack evidence that selected heads truly measure bias, using Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B as examples.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should question bias-removal claims that rely solely on head ablation without solid bias evidence.

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.summary: Higher benchmark scores for coding models don’t guarantee increased real-world productivity, as shown by a recent export ban forcing users to switch models.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should question benchmark relevance when evaluating coding AI for practical use.

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
items.summary: The paper introduces ID‑MAE, a multimodal masked‑diffusion autoencoder that self‑supervisedly predicts driver impairment using cognitive, gaze, and behavioral data.
items.whyItMatters: It enables scalable, label‑efficient driver‑assistance systems that adapt to subtle cognitive states.

items.title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
items.summary: The paper introduces a distortion‑free semantic watermarking method for black‑box generative models, guaranteeing no change to output distribution.
items.whyItMatters: It enables secure model tracking without compromising generation quality, crucial for AI deployment and compliance.

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The paper reveals that vision-language models can inadvertently assist harmful actions by interpreting scene states and introduces a benchmark to test this vulnerability.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should know VLMs can enable unsafe behavior, impacting AI safety and policy.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.summary: Fine-tuning Gemma 4 edge models on a laptop’s iGPU for MATLAB DSP code using SFT, LoRA, and QLoRA to reduce systematic errors.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how lightweight LLMs can be adapted for accurate, offline signal‑processing development on consumer hardware.

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary: The paper introduces Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a federated system for verifying identity, integrity, and authorization of AI agents across organizations.
items.whyItMatters: It enables secure, trustworthy collaboration between autonomous agents from different entities.

items.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
items.summary: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz. We study whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops…

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.summary: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither…

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. items.title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI
items.summary: We investigate how language models process negation in natural language inference (NLI). We propose the Polarity Composition Hypothesis, a high-level causal model of this computation. Behavioral evaluations show that language-model predictions largely conform to the proposed hypothesis. items.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by…

items.title: Déjà View: A Shared Working-Memory Model for Visual Tasks
items.summary: A working-memory model must remember stimuli and use its memory flexibly to perform different tasks. Here we introduce a model of working memory for images that combines dynamic activity with temporary associations between image features. We train the model on five tasks, including remembering a sample while other images are presented, categorizing distractor images while remembering the sample…

items.title: Inference after coding agents
items.summary: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference.
